name: NYC Unsafe Facade Filings
pitch: Every NYC building whose Local Law 11 facade report was filed Unsafe or SWARMP in the last 30 days, for facade restoration and masonry contractors; Unsafe conditions must be repaired within 90 days and a shed goes up now.

buyer.who: facade restoration and masonry contractors working on NYC buildings over six stories
buyer.reach: DOB NOW permits name the permittee business on every FISP repair job; email through the firm's own website contact page

price.reason: One facade job runs $100,000 to over $1 million, so one won job pays years; half of BuildDocket's $199 per trade per borough

competitors.name: BuildDocket full coverage (one trade, one borough; facade is a listed trade and FISP filings a listed source)
ViolationWatch (owner side compliance alerts, per building, not a lead list)

aiQueries.q: Habitat: why unsafe facade filings rose to 13.3% of Cycle 9 filings and what repairs cost boards
Local Law 11 contractors NYC: 15 top firms (owners shopping for a facade contractor)

data.publisher: NYC Department of Buildings (NYC Open Data)
data.dataset: DOB NOW: Safety, Facades Compliance Filings (xubg-57si)
data.subject: a facade inspection filing for a building over six stories (address, BIN, status, filing date)
data.countNote: Distinct buildings (bin) filed in Sept 2026: Unsafe 82, SWARMP 80, Safe 140, no status 37. Filings by month, Unsafe: Jul 44, Aug 50, Sep 83, Oct 1 to 21 108 (Cycle 10 sub cycle A deadline is Feb 21, 2027, so volume rises into winter). Metadata: Update Frequency every weekday, automated.

license.note: NYC Open Data terms: datasets are offered for information, the City gives no warranty and is not liable for errors, and users accept the NYC.gov terms plus any extra agency terms; nothing bars commercial reuse. The Open Data Law (Local Law 11 of 2012, Admin Code 23-502(d), https://intro.nyc/local-laws/2012-11) says public datasets are offered with no registration, no license and no limits on use; the agency may ask for credit. No indemnity clause found (unlike Chicago).

overlap: launches/chicago-exterior-violations.md (exterior repair citations, on hold as thin); this is a different city and signal. Owner and engineer person names in the dataset are dropped; many buildings are co-op or condo buildings, the same question the elevator spec raised for Legal.
